summary: Sustained 5xx spike from small streaming connection fan-in causing runtime OOMs and gateway backpressure
description:
Issue summary:
Customers (Glassline Analytics, dedicated) observed a sustained elevated 5xx error rate beginning 2026-03-14 02:15 UTC. Symptoms include API gateway returning 502/503 and upstream runtimes reporting OOMs and repeated worker restarts.

Impact:
- Multiple customer endpoints intermittently returning 5xx, affecting production inference for short-streaming requests and small-payload embed calls.
- Error rate peak ~14% of requests for a 30-minute window, downstream retries caused increased load.
- Customer reports degraded throughput & timeouts for real-time event enrichment pipeline.

Environment:
- Region: us-east (prod)
- Tier: Dedicated capacity pool (tenant pinned to model redwood/open-4b-int8)
- API surface: streaming API and short request text generation (avg payload 80 tokens)

Steps to reproduce (internal reproduction):
1) Run a synthetic load generator sending many concurrent short-lived streaming sessions (50ms per connect, ~2000 sessions/min) to the tenant's route.
2) Observe apigw accept queue growth and many ephemeral TCP connections.
3) Observe runtimes allocate KV cache for new sessions and free frequently; GPU memory fragmentation increases and NVML reports cudaFree warnings.
4) After ~5-10 minutes, runtimes hit OOM watchdog -> worker restart -> upstream 5xx responses.

Observed behavior:
- apigw logs: repeated 502/503 for tenant routes with "upstream reset" and "no healthy upstream" bursts.
- runtime logs: repeated "GPU memory allocation failed" and "watchdog: OOM -> restarting worker" entries.
- metrics: GPU memory fragmentation metric increases from baseline ~8% to ~42% during spike; runtime restart count +10 in 10 minutes.
- kvcache: high eviction rate and frequent cold-shard reloads.

Expected behavior:
- Short-lived streaming sessions should be multiplexed onto healthy long-lived workers; backpressure should be handled by ingress prioritizer without causing kernel-level GPU OOMs.

Temporary mitigations performed so far:
- Support adjusted apigw keepalive and connection reuse policy for the tenant to prefer longer pooled connections (rolled config at 2026-03-14 02:42 UTC).
- Reduced tenant concurrency cap from 600 -> 300 while we investigate.
- Applied emergency rate-shed rule to small-payload streaming route to reduce fan-in to runtimes.

Next steps (action items):
- Engineering to correlate NVML traces to runtime memory allocator activity and evaluate fragmentation pattern.
- Verify ingress prioritizer fairness settings and fix misapplied small-stream classification rule.
- Consider KV cache warmup persistence for tenant to avoid repeated allocations.
- Post-incident: follow-up runbook updates to catch short-connection storm patterns and automatic tuned rate-shed thresholds.

2026-03-14 03:45 UTC - Runtime Eng (Liam OConnell): Found repeated cudaFree failures on worker x86-prod-rt-14; fragmentation metric rose quickly. Hypothesis: frequent KV cache allocate/free due to ephemeral streaming sessions.
2026-03-14 04:12 UTC - Support (Ayesha Patel): Applied temporary lower concurrency cap for tenant and adjusted keepalive pooling. Error rate dropped to ~3% from 14% after change.
2026-03-14 04:30 UTC - Customer (Glassline Analytics - Erin Cho): Noted reduced errors but slower throughput. Asking for ETA on permanent fix.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: small short-lived streaming sessions bypassing connection reuse cause frequent KV cache allocations, inducing GPU memory fragmentation and OOMs. Evidence: NVML logs show multiple cudaMalloc/cudaFree cycles coincident with kvcache eviction spike. Correlated metrics: runtime_worker_restarts, gpu_memory_fragmentation, apigw_accept_queue_depth. We validated by replaying a short-stream load in staging and reproduced fragmentation pattern. Apigw config had 'short_stream_threshold' at 40ms for this tenant incorrectly set to 0, which prevented multiplexing into pooled streams. Also saw priority classifier mis-tagging these sessions as low priority, causing them to get scheduled onto ephemeral workers rather than warm pool. Logged related stack traces and attached NVML snippets to PR referenced in related_github_prs.
resolution_notes: Workaround applied: adjusted apigw pooling/keepalive settings and temporarily lowered tenant concurrency cap which reduced error rate. Engineering plan: fix short_stream_threshold classification bug and update ingress prioritizer to prefer pooling for <200 token sessions. A hotfix PR (runtime/pull/4216) created to persist small-session KV cache and reduce allocate/free churn; target rollout to canary 2026-03-15 02:00 UTC, full rollout after verification. Post-incident action: add automated synthetic test that simulates high-rate short streaming sessions and alert when fragmentation > 25%.
